items: Use Terraform to provision resources across two cloud providers.
Structure reusable infrastructure with modules and input variables.
Manage provider configuration and state separation per environment.
Apply the same module to different providers via variable-driven design.
Validate a multi-cloud deployment end to end.
Provider — a Terraform plugin (aws, google, azurerm) that talks to a cloud API.
Module — a reusable, parameterized bundle of resources (the "abstraction unit").
Variable / Output — inputs and return values that parameterize and expose module data.
Backend — where Terraform stores state (local, S3, GCS, remote).
Multi-cloud — running workloads on >1 provider for resilience or capability fit.

blocks.text: Provision a "hello world" web endpoint on AWS (an S3-backed static site or EC2) and a counterpart on Google Cloud (a GCS bucket or GCE instance) using a single Terraform project with a shared module. The module accepts a provider_name and region, abstracting differences.

A root configuration declares two providers and calls one web_node module twice — once per cloud — with different region and instance_type variables. State is stored in each provider's native object store (S3 for AWS, GCS for GCP) to respect blast-radius isolation.

items: Terraform >= 1.5 installed.
AWS and GCP accounts with credentials (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS).
Two empty buckets (S3 + GCS) for remote state.

blocks.text: Create modules/web_node/main.tf with a variable "cloud" (aws|gcp), variable "region", variable "name". Use count/for_each or provider aliases to branch resource creation.
Define variables.tf (region, project, instance_type) and outputs.tf exporting endpoint URLs from each module.
Run terraform init, terraform plan, terraform apply. Confirm both resources exist via cloud consoles and terraform state list.

items: A Terraform project with modules/web_node, root main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf.
Successful terraform apply on both providers (paste terraform state list showing AWS + GCP resources).
A README explaining how to add a third cloud by reusing the module.
Bonus: add a tflint/validation block enforcing allowed regions.
